title: Kangaroo Tail candlestick pattern detector
description: A 3-bar reversal pattern from Elder ch. 20 ('fingers'), completely separate from anything in this codebase (no candlestick-pattern detection exists at all). Definition, purely from OHLC: a single bar whose range is roughly 2-3x the recent average bar range, protruding from a tight recent range, where the close ends up back near the open (not at the extreme) -- flanked by two bars of normal height. An upward-pointing tail (new high, closes back down) = bearish reversal; a downward-pointing tail (new low, closes back up) = bullish reversal. Stop placement is explicit in the source: halfway through the tail, not at its tip (too wide) or base (too tight) -- expose this as a suggested reference level alongside the flag, not just a boolean.

checklist.step: Decide and record the exact 'average bar range' baseline (lookback window, and the multiplier threshold for what counts as a tail -- book says roughly 2-3x, pick and justify a specific number).
Implement detection for both directions (upward/downward tail) plus the confirming-next-bar check.
Implement the halfway-through-the-tail suggested stop reference.
Tests reproducing the book's own worked examples (BIIB upward tail, FDO downward tail) as closely as fixture data allows.
Expose as a flag (+ direction + suggested stop reference) on the analysis/indicator-history responses; regenerate openapi.json/frontend types; document in docs/Analyse.md.

decisions.decision: Detection algorithm (app.signals.kangaroo_tail.detect_kangaroo_tails): (1) baseline 'average bar range' is the mean high-low over the 10 trading days (~2 weeks) immediately preceding the candidate bar; (2) a candidate qualifies as tail-sized if its own range is >= 2.5x that baseline (the midpoint of the book's own 'roughly 2-3x') AND its high/low is a genuine new extreme beyond the whole 10-day lookback window's own high/low, not just wider than its own bars; (3) both the tail bar's open AND close must retrace >= 50% of the bar's own range back from the tip (new high/low), for 'the close ends up back near the open, not at the extreme'; (4) the bar immediately before AND immediately after must each themselves fail the same 2.5x tail-sized test (reused, not a second invented threshold) for 'flanked by two bars of normal height'.
decisions.rationale: The book (Elder ch. 20, per docs/ideas.md) describes the shape precisely -- 'roughly 2-3x the recent average bar range', 'protruding from a tight recent range', 'close ends up back near the open, not at the extreme', 'flanked by two bars of normal height' -- but gives no mechanical algorithm, exactly the situation this task's own checklist item 1 flags as a judgment call to make and record, and the same situation app.signals.support_resistance was in for its own zone-detection algorithm (an explicit precedent for how this app resolves 'concept precise, mechanism not' cases). 10 trading days (~2 weeks) is a reasonable, small baseline window long enough to establish a genuine 'recent average' without being so long it dilutes a real regime change into noise; no book-given number exists for this, so it's this app's own choice, kept deliberately short given 'recent' is the book's own word. 2.5x (the midpoint of the book's own explicit 2-3x range) is the most literal, defensible single number to pick from a stated range with no further guidance on which end is more correct. The 50% retracement threshold is the natural midpoint reading of 'ends up back near the open, not at the extreme' -- requiring the body to sit in the FAR half of the range from the tip is a direct, checkable formalization of that qualitative description, and requiring it of BOTH open and close (not close alone) is what actually captures 'close near the OPEN' as a relationship between the two, not just 'close away from the extreme' on its own. Reusing the same 2.5x threshold for the flanking-bar 'normal height' check (rather than inventing a second, lower number) keeps the parameter surface minimal and is textually justified: 'normal' simply means 'not itself a tail-sized outlier', which is exactly what the tail's own qualification test already measures. A small baseline value is itself treated as satisfying 'protruding from a tight recent range' -- no separate volatility-tightness check was added, since a range-multiplier test against a small recent average already IS a test for stickng out of a tight range; a genuinely wide/choppy recent window would produce a large baseline, making the multiplier test correspondingly harder to satisfy, so the two concepts (tightness, protrusion) aren't actually separable requirements here. Rejected alternatives: (a) a longer lookback (e.g. 20 trading days, matching Kerry Lovvorn's divergence-spacing lower bound) -- rejected as no more textually grounded than 10 and slower to react to a genuine recent volatility regime, which 'recent' argues against; (b) picking 2.0x or 3.0x (either endpoint of the book's stated range) instead of the midpoint -- rejected as arbitrarily favoring one end with no textual reason to prefer it over the other; (c) a separate, lower flanking-bar threshold (e.g. 1.5x) distinct from the tail's own 2.5x qualifying threshold -- rejected as inventing a second unstated number when the book's own language ('normal height', i.e. not itself an outlier) is already fully captured by the existing threshold.

decisions.decision: The confirming-next-bar check is implemented as a HARD GATE, not an informational flag: detect_kangaroo_tails only ever returns a KangarooTail once its confirming bar (i) has a normal, non-tail-sized range AND (ii) closes in the direction the reversal implies (below the tail's own close for an upward/bearish tail, above it for a downward/bullish one). A shape-matching candidate whose confirming bar fails either check is not returned at all -- there is no `confirmed: bool` field on a partially-qualifying candidate.
decisions.rationale: The checklist phrases this as an explicit, separate thing to 'implement' beyond plain shape detection ('Implement detection for both directions... plus the confirming-next-bar check'), and Elder's own methodology throughout this codebase already treats a next-bar confirmation requirement as a hard precondition for a pattern to count as a genuine trading signal at all, not a weaker version of one -- the closest, most direct precedent is app.signals.divergence's MACD-Histogram centerline-crossing rule ('an absolute must for a true divergence... no crossover, no divergence at all, not merely a weaker one'), which this app already implements as a hard filter rather than an exposed-but-optional flag. Since the confirming bar (the second flanking bar) is already REQUIRED data for the 3-bar shape itself (flanked by two bars of normal height), no additional look-ahead or later data is needed to evaluate the confirmation condition at the same time -- there's no meaningful 'candidate detected, confirmation still pending' state to expose in the first place, since both properties of that same bar are knowable together the moment it exists. Rejected alternative: return every shape-matching candidate with a `confirmed: bool` field (mirroring Divergence's own non-gating `aborted`/`beyond_reference_line` informational booleans) -- rejected because, unlike those, the confirmation check here doesn't depend on possibly-distant future data the shape detection didn't already need; making it non-gating would only ever produce `confirmed=True` results in practice (since the same bar is already mandatory for the flanking-bar check), so a boolean field would be redundant noise rather than genuinely informative.

decisions.decision: suggested_stop = the tail bar's own range midpoint, (high + low) / 2, for BOTH directions (not a separate open/close-based formula).
decisions.rationale: The book's own explicit rule is 'halfway through the tail, not at its tip (too wide) or its base (too tight)'. Reading the tip as the bar's own extreme (high for an upward tail, low for a downward one) and the base as the OPPOSITE end of the same range is the most literal interpretation available -- and it's specifically justified here (not just assumed) because this task's own body-position requirement (decision above, point 3) already constrains both open and close to sit in that opposite half of the range, i.e. near that same 'base' end. This makes the bar's own high-low midpoint a faithful 'halfway through the tail' reference without inventing a second, less-grounded formula keyed off open/close instead of high/low. Rejected alternatives: (a) a formula based on the body's own midpoint (e.g. (open+close)/2, offset toward the tip by some fraction) -- rejected as needing an additional invented fraction/offset parameter the book doesn't give, where the plain range midpoint already satisfies the book's own 'halfway through the tail' language directly and requires no extra parameter; (b) treating the base as the body's near edge instead of the bar's own opposite extreme -- rejected as a narrower, more model-dependent definition of 'base' than 'the tail's own range midpoint', which is unambiguous and independently computable from OHLC alone.

decisions.decision: Confirmed via grep (docs/ideas.md, docs/Analyse.md) that no numeric OHLC transcription of the book's own BIIB/FDO chart examples exists anywhere in this repo's docs -- the checklist's reference to them describes the book's real, named examples, not data already captured here. tests/unit/signals/test_kangaroo_tail.py's TestBIIBAndFDOWorkedExamples class builds synthetic fixtures reproducing each example's QUALITATIVE shape (BIIB: an upward tail spiking to a new high after a tight consolidation, closing back down -- flagged bearish; FDO: the downward mirror, flagged bullish) rather than a numeric transcription of the real historical charts, and documents this substitution explicitly in the test class's own docstring.
decisions.rationale: This mirrors the exact precedent set by backend-divergence-detection's own task (docs/tasks/done/backend-divergence-detection.json's decisions), which found the same situation for its own checklist's claimed 'DJIA 2007-2009' chart example -- also not actually present in the docs -- and resolved it the same way: hand-computed synthetic fixtures covering the pattern's real filter boundaries, with the substitution stated plainly rather than presenting an invented numeric series as if it were the book's own real data. Fabricating a plausible-looking BIIB/FDO price series from memory and presenting it as ground truth would misrepresent an unverifiable claim as fact, which CLAUDE.md's decision-memory/honesty expectations and the add-indicator skill's reference-value-test bar both argue against; skipping a dedicated BIIB/FDO-shaped test entirely would leave this checklist item's explicit request unaddressed. The chosen synthetic fixtures (tests/unit/signals/test_kangaroo_tail.py's _up_tail_overrides/_down_tail_overrides, reused directly by TestBIIBAndFDOWorkedExamples) are the same fully hand-computed, reference-value fixtures the rest of that test file already uses, so the substitution doesn't come at the cost of a weaker test than the rest of the suite.

decisions.decision: AnalysisResponse.kangaroo_tail / each IndicatorHistoryPoint.kangaroo_tail expose the single MOST RECENTLY CONFIRMED tail as a persisting 'current state' (matching AnalysisResponse.divergence's own convention) rather than a sparse one-shot marker that only appears non-null on the exact bar it was confirmed. The nested KangarooTailOut schema names the tail bar's own date field `tail_date`, not `date` (unlike GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators' own top-level per-point `date` field), because Pydantic v2 raises a real `PydanticUserError` ('field name clashing with a type annotation') when a model has a field literally named `date` typed `date` followed by ANOTHER field also typed `date` -- the second field's own `date` annotation resolves against the class body's own (by-then-already-bound) `date` field name instead of the module-level `datetime.date` import, since this file has no `from __future__ import annotations`. Kangaroo Tail detection + exposure is NOT wired into `_determine_signal`, the Impulse gate, or confidence scoring.
decisions.rationale: Persisting 'current state' semantics were chosen over a sparse per-bar marker because that's the established, already-reviewed precedent this codebase uses for every other 'detect an event, then report its ongoing relevance' signal on these same two endpoints (Divergence, and Indicator Seasons' own timeline in spirit) -- introducing a second, different exposure convention just for this one pattern would be a real, unjustified inconsistency for a consuming client (and the not-yet-implemented frontend-kangaroo-tail-markers task, already on the board, can derive 'this is a NEW tail' itself by diffing consecutive points' `tail_date`, the same way frontend-divergence-markers already had to for Divergence). Confirmed empirically (a real `PydanticUserError` reproduced and fixed during implementation, not a hypothetical) that a field literally named `date` cannot safely coexist with a second `date`-typed field in the same Pydantic model in this codebase's style (no `from __future__ import annotations`) -- `tail_date` avoids the collision entirely and matches this app's own existing sibling-schema convention of never using a bare `date` field name inside a nested object (FalseBreakoutOut uses `breakout_date`/`reentry_date`, DivergenceOut uses `first_extreme_date`/`second_extreme_date` -- neither uses a bare `date` field, which in hindsight is presumably why neither ever hit this same Pydantic error). Not wiring into `_determine_signal`/the Impulse gate/confidence scoring matches this task's own description (an explicit standalone pattern) and the identical scope precedent every sibling detection task (support_resistance, divergence, seasons) already established -- detection + exposure only, with methodology-level integration left as a deliberate, separate follow-up decision for a later task if ever wanted. Rejected alternatives: (a) a sparse per-bar marker (non-null only on the bar where a tail's own `confirmed_date` falls) -- rejected for the consistency reason above, and because it would make `AnalysisResponse.kangaroo_tail` (the latest-bar-only snapshot) usually null even when a still-recent, still-relevant tail exists just a few bars back, an inconsistent asymmetry with how `divergence` behaves on that same response; (b) naming the field `date` and instead reordering the schema's fields to dodge the Pydantic collision (e.g. put the `date`-named field last) -- rejected as a fragile ordering-dependent workaround that would silently break again the moment any field were reordered or a new one added before it, versus `tail_date`'s permanent, self-documenting fix that also matches this app's own established sibling-schema naming convention.

comments.summary: backend/app/signals/kangaroo_tail.py verified: 10-day lookback / 2.5x range multiplier / 50% retracement thresholds are reasonable, textually-grounded readings of the book's 'roughly 2-3x' (2.5 is the literal midpoint) with no arbitrary unjustified numbers; the confirming-next-bar check is a genuine hard gate (a shape-matching candidate whose confirming bar fails either the normal-range or direction-continuation check returns None, never a confirmed=False record); suggested_stop=(high+low)/2 matches Elder's 'halfway through the tail, not tip or base' guidance exactly, and is specifically justified by the body-retracement requirement already constraining open/close to the opposite half of the range. No look-ahead bias in the analyse_history precompute path: build_kangaroo_tail_cache/kangaroo_tail_confirmed_as_of filters by confirming-bar positional index <= the current bar, verified directly by a dedicated test (test_engine.py's test_kangaroo_tail_appears_only_from_its_confirming_bar_onward_no_look_ahead) proving the tail is invisible to every bar before its own confirming bar. The BIIB/FDO fixture-substitution claim (decisions entry 4) is accurate -- grepped docs/ideas.md and docs/Analyse.md myself and confirmed no numeric OHLC transcription of either example exists; the synthetic-fixture substitution is documented plainly in the test class's own docstring, mirroring the backend-divergence-detection precedent. The tail_date (not date) field rename is a sound fix for a real, independently-reproduced PydanticUserError (confirmed by reproducing the exact collision in a standalone script: a field literally named `date` followed by a second date-typed field raises 'field name clashing with a type annotation' in this codebase's Pydantic v2/no-future-annotations style).

Full suites pass: backend 740 passed, 99.92% coverage (kangaroo_tail.py itself 100%); frontend 492 passed (one PortfolioPage.test.tsx timeout on the first full-suite run was confirmed a pre-existing flake unrelated to this PR -- passes standalone and on a clean re-run of the full suite), ~99.7% coverage. ruff, mypy, eslint, and tsc all clean. Regenerated backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts myself from the checked-out branch and diffed against the committed versions -- both are byte-identical, confirming the snapshots are genuinely in sync, not stale. docs/Analyse.md row 13 and docs/architecture/{API,Backend}.md are updated consistently with the implementation. No frontend UI component consumes kangaroo_tail yet (this task is detection+exposure only, matching its sibling tasks' scope; a separate frontend-kangaroo-tail-markers task already exists on the board for the UI) -- confirmed via grep that no non-test frontend file references it, so per step 9/9a this PR has no UI surface: browser walkthrough and the e2e suite were both skipped, explicitly, rather than silently omitted.

Non-blocking (code-review, medium effort): app.signals.kangaroo_tail.build_kangaroo_tail_cache's get_loc(tail.confirmed_date) lacks the isinstance(position, int) guard against a non-unique index that the identical pattern in app.signals.divergence has -- currently unreachable (this app's daily-bar indices are always unique, same premise divergence.py's own guard relies on) but an inconsistency with established sibling-module defensive style. Filed as a follow-up.

Non-blocking (code-review, medium effort): the code comment for the new-high/new-low outside-bar tie-break ('"up" takes priority in that degenerate tie... See this task's decisions entry') cites a decisions entry that does not actually exist -- none of the 5 recorded decisions discuss this tie-break, and there is no test exercising the case where a bar is simultaneously a new high AND a new low beyond the lookback window. Filed as a follow-up to either record the decision properly or correct the comment, plus add a regression test.
